title: fix: auto-fill pubkey in signEvent
body:
## Summary
- `signEvent()` now auto-fills `pubkey` from `getPublicKey()` when the caller omits it
- Matches the behavior of NIP-07 and nsec signers which set pubkey automatically
- Uses the cached pubkey from v1.1.0's `getPublicKey()` cache — no extra API call

## Problem
Callers (like divine-web's `useNostrPublish`) pass events without `pubkey` because NIP-46 signers are expected to fill it in. The REST RPC signer was forwarding the event as-is, causing `login.divine.video/api/nostr` to return 400 "Invalid event format: missing field pubkey".

This broke all event publishing (view counts, reactions, follows, etc.) for JWT-authenticated users.

## Test plan
- [x] 44 existing tests pass
- [x] Lint clean
- [x] Build succeeds
- [ ] Verify divine-web view count events (Kind 22236) publish successfully with updated SDK

Bumps to v1.1.1.

title: feat: harden DivineRpc with production robustness features
body:
## Summary

Adds production-hardening features to `DivineRpc` ported from divine-signer's battle-tested `OAuthSigner`:

- **AbortSignal timeout** (30s) on all fetch calls
- **RpcError** class with `.status` property, exported from package
- **429 retry** with exponential backoff + Retry-After header support (max 3 retries)
- **Pubkey caching** in `getPublicKey()` — avoids duplicate HTTP calls (signEvent calls getPublicKey internally)
- **onUnauthorized hook** — optional callback for 401 refresh delegation with coalesced concurrent refresh
- **NIP-46 compliant signEvent** — `JSON.stringify(event)` instead of raw object
- **CI workflow** — GitHub Actions running lint, test, and build

## Notes

- Only 401 triggers refresh (not 403 — that means policy denied, not token expired)
- `onUnauthorized` returns a new access token string; DivineRpc doesn't know about OAuth refresh tokens
- `createDivineClient` factory doesn't wire `onUnauthorized` — consumers needing auto-refresh construct `DivineRpc` directly

## Testing

19 new tests in `tests/rpc.test.ts`, all 44 tests passing.
